summary.en: Describe entities, attributes and relationship rules with Chen notation.
summary.bn: চেন নোটেশনে এনটিটি, অ্যাট্রিবিউট ও সম্পর্কের নিয়ম প্রকাশ করো।

notes: CHECK constraints are enforced from MySQL 8.0.16. The examples also run on MySQL 8.4.

sections.title: Draw the rules before building tables
Make the drawing say something precise

practice.title: Classify student facts
practice.statementHtml: Classify student_id, address, phone numbers and age as attribute kinds.
hints: One attribute may have parts, several values or a calculation.
practice.answerHtml: student_id can be a simple key attribute. Address is composite when street, city and postcode matter separately. Phone numbers are multivalued. Age is derived from birth date and a specified date, so storing it risks stale values.

practice.title: State both limits
practice.statementHtml: Each section must have one teacher. A teacher may teach no sections or many. State minimum and maximum participation.
hints: Write the rule separately from each end.
practice.answerHtml: Section has minimum 1 and maximum 1 teacher, so its participation is total. Teacher has minimum 0 and maximum many sections, so participation is partial. The maximum cardinality is teacher 1:N section.

practice.title: Draw a weak entity
practice.statementHtml: Building numbers are unique, but room numbers are unique only within a building. Describe the Chen diagram.
hints: Try identifying room 101 without naming its building.
practice.answerHtml: Draw Building as a rectangle with underlined building_id. Draw Room as a double rectangle with dashed-underlined room_number as partial key. Connect them with a double-diamond identifying relationship. Room participates totally; its identifier is building_id together with room_number.

practice.title: Attach a relationship attribute
practice.statementHtml: A student earns marks in a section. Should marks belong directly to Student or Section?
hints: Ask which pair determines one mark value.
practice.answerHtml: Neither alone identifies the event. Marks describe the student-section enrollment, so attach marks to the relationship or to an enrollment entity. Putting marks on Student loses the section; putting them on Section loses the student.

practice.title: Choose relationship degree
practice.statementHtml: A supplier provides a book to a branch at an agreed price. Explain why three independent binary links may lose meaning.
hints: Do the binary links preserve the same combinations?
practice.answerHtml: The price may depend on the particular supplier-book-branch combination. Separate supplier-book and book-branch links do not record which supplier serves that branch at that price. Keep the ternary fact unless additional business rules justify a binary decomposition.

quiz.prompt: In Chen notation, which shape represents an entity type?
quiz.explanation: Rectangles name entity types; diamonds label relationship types.

quiz.prompt: Which Chen shape represents an attribute?
quiz.explanation: An oval labels an attribute attached to its entity or relationship.

quiz.prompt: How is a multivalued phone attribute normally drawn?
quiz.explanation: A double oval means several values may belong to one entity.

quiz.prompt: Why is age often a derived attribute?
options: It is always a composite key
It can be calculated from birth date and a reference date
quiz.explanation: Age depends on another stored fact and the date of calculation.

options: It can be divided into street, city and postcode
quiz.explanation: Composite describes meaningful parts, not multiple whole values.

quiz.prompt: A student enrolls in many sections and each section has many students. What is the cardinality?
quiz.explanation: Both ends allow several partners, so a bridge will later be needed.

quiz.prompt: What does total participation say about a teacher assigned to a department?
options: The department has exactly one teacher
Every teacher must participate in that relationship
The teacher is a weak entity
quiz.explanation: Total participation is a minimum rule, distinct from the maximum number of partners.

quiz.prompt: What identifies room 101 when room numbers repeat between buildings?
quiz.explanation: The owner key combines with a partial key to identify a weak room.

quiz.prompt: What is the degree of a relationship involving Student, Course and Semester?
quiz.explanation: Degree counts participating entity types, not instances.

quiz.prompt: How is an identifying relationship for a weak entity shown in Chen notation?
options: A single underline on every attribute
quiz.explanation: A double diamond connects the weak entity to its identifying owner.

keyPoints.en: Entities are distinguishable things within your chosen scope.
keyPoints.bn: তোমার কাজের পরিসরে আলাদা করে চেনা যায় এমন বিষয়ই এনটিটি।

keyPoints.en: Composite attributes can be split into useful parts.
keyPoints.bn: কম্পোজিট অ্যাট্রিবিউটকে অর্থপূর্ণ ছোট অংশে ভাগ করা যায়।

keyPoints.en: Cardinality sets a relationship’s maximum participation.
keyPoints.bn: কার্ডিনালিটি সম্পর্কে অংশগ্রহণের সর্বোচ্চ সংখ্যা জানায়।

keyPoints.en: Total participation requires every entity to join the relationship.
keyPoints.bn: টোটাল পার্টিসিপেশনে প্রতিটি এনটিটিকে সম্পর্কে থাকতে হয়।

keyPoints.en: A weak entity needs its owner’s key for identification.
keyPoints.bn: উইক এনটিটিকে শনাক্ত করতে মালিক এনটিটির কি লাগে।

examQuestions.question: Explain cardinality and participation using Department and Student.
examQuestions.answerHtml: If each student belongs to exactly one department and departments may initially have no students, cardinality is Department 1:N Student. Student participation is total; Department participation is partial. A double line marks total participation in Chen notation. Maximum and minimum rules answer different questions.

examQuestions.question: Draw Chen notation for Book, Member and borrowing, including a due date.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
[Member] M --- <Borrows> --- N [Book]
                     |
                 (due_on)

The diamond represents borrowing and the oval represents its due date. Repeated loans by one member for one book need an event identifier or a loan entity; a single member-book pair cannot distinguish borrowing dates.

examQuestions.question: Distinguish simple, composite, multivalued and derived attributes.
examQuestions.answerHtml: A simple attribute has no useful parts in the chosen design, such as a student number. Address may have city and postcode parts. Several phone numbers form a multivalued attribute. Age can be derived from birth date. These classifications describe different properties, so a complex design can combine them.
